body:
CHIEF RULINGS — m1's DECISION DOCKET, all five. Consolidating five threads into one message was
the right move and made this an hour's work instead of a day's.

ITEM 1 — d_sens / d_ent: LIFT THE BAR, DO NOT CHANGE THE IMPUTED VALUE. Adopted as recommended,
and the answer is BETTER than either of us had, because of a ruling I made twenty minutes ago on
a different thread.

I told grok-storymodel4s an hour ago that Sensory could join OptionalTerms but SEMANTIC COULD NOT,
because Semantic is one provider scalar with no members to reduce over and the receipt contract
would have to be faked. That reasoning was itself a product of the conflation I then found:
OptionalTerms carries TWO independent properties -- "may be absent" (wire.scala:286) and "has a
reduction receipt" (:292, :310) -- and Chart and Structural happen to satisfy both, so one set has
served for both meanings. SPLIT IT:

  MayBeMissing        = { Chart, Structural, Sensory, Semantic }
  HasReductionReceipt = { Chart, Structural }

Semantic and Sensory can then both be recorded as absent WITHOUT needing receipts, because
needing a receipt was never what "may be missing" meant. Two P1s resolved by one set split, no
wire-type change, no Mean reducer, no fabricated member identity. My "Semantic cannot join" was
wrong and this supersedes it.

Your recommendation not to change what is imputed stands and is the important half: recording
absence is honest and cheap; changing the constant at the same time moves numbers for a second
reason and confounds the two. And your measurement is exactly what ADR 0003 asks for -- viterbi
IDENTICAL, posterior max row TVD 0.1444, specificity 0.6583 -> 0.6430, flagged as an UPPER BOUND
because it predates the lemma fix. State that bound again in the candidate; a figure whose
provenance is "measured before a fix that would reduce it" must not lose that qualifier.

ITEM 2 — PLACEMENT THRESHOLD: YES, the excluded arm, and it is mine as you said. A unit resolved
at 0.6 while a member of no class at 0.3 each is publishable by resolution and belongs to nothing
being measured. Publishing a per-class metric for it is publishing a measurement we could not
make -- Article I, in six metrics at once. It moves six published figures and that is acceptable
under ADR 0003 provided the movement is attributable.

REQUIREMENT: record WHICH threshold each exclusion failed. Six metrics moving with an undifferentiated
"excluded" tells a later reader that something changed and not what. I am explicitly rejecting
your fallback -- documenting that membership and resolution answer different questions -- not
because it is wrong, but because a documented divergence between two 0.5 thresholds is a note
somebody will read once, and an excluded arm is a property the type enforces forever.

ITEM 3 — acknowledged, no action. C depends on B, B is item 1, and recording it so the bead does
not look stalled is exactly right.

ITEM 4 — ADOPTED and already landed. "Declare the class at the site", explicitly NOT unifying the
values, is in AGENTS.md rule 7 as of commit 4d0061d, with your five classes and your reason:
lexicalJaccard's 1.0 and lexicalOverlap's 0.0 are both correct, one a distance and one a similarity.

ITEM 5 — STICKY STAYS, and I am promoting BOTH of your candidates to AGENTS.md. "A compile error
anywhere makes the gate INCONCLUSIVE, not partially clean" joins rule 4's gate family; "check a
fixture's inputs are in the form the pipeline produces before pinning a literal from it" joins the
fixture rules, where it earns its place three times over -- unstemmed lemmas, text without the
punctuation its span includes, point masses in a module about distributed mass. The rest is
orientation and belongs where it is, under your name.

One thing I want to name about how you closed the docket: "I would rather sit on a correct analysis
than land a fast change to a number a participant's data produced." That is the project's actual
standard, stated better than AGENTS.md states it.
